stories.stand: The company says an internal system was accidentally exposed to the internet during a 2025 migration; it is still working out who was affected.
body: DigiCert, a major issuer of website security certificates, has confirmed unauthorised access to an internal system holding archived customer information, Cyber Security News reported.
The exposed records included names, business email addresses, phone numbers and addresses. For a small minority of accounts, they also included passports, driving licences or utility bills.
DigiCert says a network migration in February 2025 exposed the system to the internet without a security review. Outsiders created accounts and could read data between 27 June and 2 July 2026.

The company says its certificate services were not affected and customers do not need to replace certificates. It has not said how many people were affected, and says it will notify them after a review.

stories.stand: The European Chip Design Platform offers grants of up to €16 million; EU auditors doubt the bloc will meet its 2030 chip production goal.
body: The European Commission launched the European Chip Design Platform on Wednesday, with €525 million for early-stage chip start-ups and small firms, Euronews reported.
Grants of up to €16 million will pay for design tools, access to intellectual property and access to manufacturing. The Commission says European firms earn less than 1% of global chip-design revenue.

The EU Chips Act aims for 20% of global chip production by 2030, up from about 9% in 2020. The European Court of Auditors said in 2025 that this was very unlikely to be met.

stories.say: SpaceX has chosen Qualcomm chips for the base stations of Starlink Mobile, its planned nationwide 5G phone network in the US, with the rollout due to begin in 2027.
stories.stand: The multi-year deal moves SpaceX closer to running its own US mobile network, using ground masts in cities and satellites elsewhere.
body: SpaceX has chosen Qualcomm's Dragonwing chips for the base stations in Starlink Mobile, a planned nationwide 5G network in the US, Not a Tesla App reported.
The multi-year deal's financial terms were not disclosed. SpaceX plans tens of thousands of cell sites, with the rollout beginning in 2027.

body: Channel 4 says Married at First Sight UK will not return, following an external review launched after allegations from former contestants.

Two women alleged their on-screen husbands raped them, and a third accused her on-screen husband of sexual misconduct. The men deny the allegations. The claims were first reported by the BBC, and Channel 4 removed past series from its streaming service in May.

The review had two parts. Law firm Clyde & Co found no breach of Ofcom's code but noted isolated lapses in the welfare framework. Former BBC executive Lorraine Heggessey rated the welfare protocols highly.

Chief executive Priya Dogra said applying all the recommendations would fundamentally change the format, and that the show had run its course after 10 years. A series filmed this year will not be broadcast. Producer CPL said contributor welfare had always been central to its work.

stories.stand: The company managing the late singer's business filed to dismiss its case against Bryan Seaver, her former head of security, without prejudice.
body: The company that manages Dolly Parton's business interests, She's Alive, filed a notice in Tennessee state court on Thursday to voluntarily dismiss its lawsuit against her nephew, Bryan Seaver.

Seaver, who ran her security for about two decades through his firm Squadron Augmented Protection Services, was accused in September of making threats after Parton's death. A judge granted a temporary restraining order that month.

The dismissal is without prejudice, meaning the claims could be refiled, ABC News reported. Seaver's lawyers told CBS News he wants to put the misunderstanding behind him so the family can grieve privately.
In an 18-page filing on Monday, Seaver denied threatening anyone and said his company had been owed about $251,000, since paid. Parton died of cancer in August, aged 80.

stories.head: Prix Goncourt winner Philippe Jaenada admits using AI in his novel
stories.say: Philippe Jaenada, who won France's Prix Goncourt on Tuesday, says he put a sentence written by ChatGPT into his novel and used the chatbot for research.
stories.stand: France's top literary prize winner says he slipped a ChatGPT-written sentence into his book and used the chatbot for research, prompting debate among readers.
body: Philippe Jaenada, 62, won the Prix Goncourt, France's most prestigious literary award, on Tuesday for L'Inconnue du quai de Javel, about an unsolved murder in Paris in the late 1940s.

Speaking to France Inter on Wednesday, he said he used AI three times. He inserted a ChatGPT-written sentence to play with the reader, and told the jury which one. He also used it for technical research and to mock one of its answers.
Jaenada argued that writers should acknowledge AI rather than ignore it, while keeping it as a tool. Reaction on social media was divided.
Separately, Thélyson Orélien's novel was removed from the Goncourt selection over AI and plagiarism accusations. His publisher, Éditions du Boréal, ended its work with him.

stories.head: Mahabharata and Arthashastra manuscripts join UNESCO memory register
stories.say: Manuscripts of three ancient Indian works, the Mahabharata, the Arthashastra and the Rajatarangini, have been added to a UNESCO regional register of documentary heritage.
stories.stand: Manuscripts of three ancient Indian works have been added to UNESCO's Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register, India's culture ministry says.
body: Manuscripts of the Mahabharata epic, Kautilya's Arthashastra on statecraft and Kalhana's 12th-century chronicle Rajatarangini have been added to UNESCO's Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Regional Register, Indian officials announced on Thursday.

The decision was taken at the register's 11th session in Jakarta, according to the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, which helped prepare the nominations. This is the regional list, not the international one.

The Mahabharata manuscript is a 400-year-old birch-bark text held at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, the Tribune reported. The Arthashastra is a 16th-century palm-leaf manuscript in Mysuru.
Culture minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat called it a landmark recognition of India's documentary heritage. An official said India now has six entries on the regional register.

body: The Metropolitan Museum of Art has named its spring 2027 Costume Institute exhibition extraORDINARY: Fashion and the Poetics of the Everyday.

The show looks at how designers transform familiar garments such as denim, T-shirts and hoodies, and materials such as paper and plastic. The Met Gala will be held on 3 May 2027, and the exhibition runs from 9 May 2027 to 9 January 2028.
It replaces John Galliano: Horizons, which the Met and the designer agreed on 31 August not to proceed with, after backlash over his past antisemitic remarks.

body: Pope Leo XIV received Bob Dylan at the Apostolic Palace on Wednesday afternoon, in what the Vatican described as a brief meeting.
The Pope gave Dylan a rosary, and Dylan gave him a copy of his autobiography, Chronicles: Volume One. The visit came between Dylan's concerts in Milan on Monday and Rome on Thursday.
Dylan was accompanied by Father Antonio Spadaro, a Vatican culture official, and Andrea Monda, editor of L'Osservatore Romano.
Leo, born in Chicago, quoted an unreleased 1963 Dylan protest song in a Vatican book on peace published this year. Dylan last performed before a pope, John Paul II, in Bologna in 1997.

The paper said the contract omitted protections in South Korea's government standard form for minors' health, education, sleep and rest. It also flagged a penalty formula and rules allowing post-contract use of members' names, faces and voices.

body: Powerhouse Parramatta, in western Sydney, opens to the public on Saturday 7 November, about seven years after the New South Wales government bought the site.
The state government puts the total budget at $915 million, including the site, storage and digitising the collection. It says more than 22,000 people have registered for opening weekend events.

body: Wall of Tears, by American artist Phil Buehler, opened at the Uniting Church Hall in Berry, New South Wales, on Thursday, drawing about 300 people, ABC News reported.
The work lists 18,457 children reported killed in Gaza between October 2023 and July 2025, according to Gaza's health ministry.

body: The Strand, the Manhattan bookstore founded in 1927, has agreed to pay $1,482,560 to resolve False Claims Act allegations, the US Justice Department announced on Tuesday.

In 2021 the shop received a $932,350 second-draw Paycheck Protection Program loan. Such loans were barred for businesses controlled by a member of Congress or their spouse. Owner Nancy Bass Wyden is married to Senator Ron Wyden.

US Attorney Jeanine Pirro said the programme was meant to save jobs, not help ineligible recipients. Bass Wyden called the error unintentional, said the rules changed rapidly, and said the money was returned.
Senator Wyden's office said he had no involvement in the loan or the settlement.

body: Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football on Thursday in a long video posted on social media. The 41-year-old's Portugal career began in August 2003.
He leaves with men's international records of 234 caps and 146 goals. He captained Portugal to the Euro 2016 title and to Nations League wins in 2019 and 2025.

The decision follows a dispute with coach Jorge Jesus over playing time. Ronaldo left the squad's training camp after being dropped to the bench. ESPN said the federation then handed him a 30-day suspension.
His last appearance was a 1-0 Nations League win over Wales on 24 September. The Portuguese Football Federation said it plans a tribute. Ronaldo will keep playing for Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia.

body: Brighton beat Getafe 1-0 in the Conference League league phase on Thursday. It was their first competitive match in Spain, ESPN reported.
Malick Yalcouyé headed in the winner in the 64th minute after Costinha nodded the ball back across goal. It was his fourth goal of the season.
Jaouen Hadjam hit the post for Brighton in the first half, and goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen made several saves for Fabian Hürzeler's side.
The win takes Brighton to seven points from three matches. ESPN said they are the only team in the competition yet to concede.

stories.head: Ferencvaros stun AC Milan 2-0 at San Siro
stories.say: Lenny Joseph scored twice as Ferencvaros won 2-0 at AC Milan on Thursday. The visitors have won all four Europa League games, while Milan have just three points.
stories.stand: Lenny Joseph scored twice as the visitors made it four wins from four, leaving Milan on three points.
body: Ferencvaros beat AC Milan 2-0 at San Siro in the Europa League on Thursday. They have won all four of their league-phase matches, while Milan have three points.
Lenny Joseph scored both goals in the second half. FotMob said the first, in the 52nd minute, came after goalkeeper Lorenzo Torriani lost control of a back pass.
Torriani, on his full debut, was starting in place of the suspended Mike Maignan. Ferencvaros substitute Bamidele Yusuf was sent off late on, but Milan could not take advantage.
Milan, coached by Ruben Amorim, had 15 shots but only two on target, FotMob reported.

stories.head: Japan's Kozo Tashima to challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency
stories.say: Japan's Kozo Tashima is to challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency. The 68-year-old FIFA Council member has his national association's backing for the vote in March.
stories.stand: The FIFA Council member is the first rival with his national association's backing; the election is due in March 2027.
body: Kozo Tashima, a former president of the Japan Football Association, intends to stand against Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency, according to reports on Thursday.
The 68-year-old has sat on the FIFA Council since 2015. ESPN, citing Japanese media, said the association's board unanimously backed his bid.
Candidates need formal support from five member associations. The election is due in March 2027; ESPN said it will be held on 18 March in Rabat, Morocco.
Infantino, seeking a fourth term, had looked set to stand unopposed, City AM reported. Former Switzerland defender Ramon Vega has also declared but is not thought to have five endorsements.

stories.head: Hamilton refuses to apologise over Leclerc clash
stories.say: Lewis Hamilton says he will not apologise for his remarks after clashing with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc in Mexico. He was speaking before Sunday's Brazilian Grand Prix.
stories.stand: Lewis Hamilton says he will not be silenced after clashing with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc in Mexico, ahead of Sunday's Brazilian Grand Prix.
body: Lewis Hamilton said on Thursday he would not apologise for comments he made after clashing with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
The pair fought on the opening lap, and Leclerc went off track at Turn 4. Hamilton said on the radio that Leclerc had pushed him off, PlanetF1 reported, and later called for rules of engagement.
Speaking ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix, Hamilton said he did not care how his remarks were viewed and would not be silenced. He said Ferrari had not asked him to stay quiet, GPblog reported.
He said he and team principal Fred Vasseur had spoken but not yet held a detailed discussion. Leclerc missed the media day after the birth of his child. The race is on Sunday.

stories.head: Chris Lynn served secret one-month ban for cocaine
stories.say: Australian batter Chris Lynn has served a one-month ban after testing positive for cocaine on T20 Blast Finals Day in July, when he was playing for Northamptonshire.
stories.stand: The Australian batter tested positive on T20 Blast Finals Day while playing for Northamptonshire; the ban has already been served.
body: Australian batter Chris Lynn, 36, has served a one-month ban after testing positive for cocaine, it emerged on Thursday. The suspension ran from 31 July to 30 August.
His sample was collected on 18 July, T20 Blast Finals Day, while he was playing for Northamptonshire, CricTracker reported. Lynn admitted using the drug in the days before.
The ECB's Cricket Regulator initially sought a three-month ban. It was reduced after Lynn completed a substance-abuse treatment programme, CricTracker said.
The use was found to be out of competition and unrelated to sporting performance, ABC News reported. Lynn, the Big Bash League's all-time leading run-scorer, is available to play.

stories.head: WTA apologises after Pegula's remarks on Andreeva are streamed
stories.say: The WTA has apologised after Jessica Pegula was heard on a livestream calling Mirra Andreeva a diva. The tour says players were not told practice microphones were live.
stories.stand: The tour says players were not told practice microphones were live at the WTA Finals; streams will now continue without audio.
body: The WTA said on Thursday it takes full responsibility after Jessica Pegula's conversation with her coach was streamed from a practice session at the WTA Finals.
Pegula was heard telling coach Mark Knowles that world number three Mirra Andreeva was a diva who needed to be humbled, Front Office Sports and Sky Sports reported.
The tour said players and teams had not been told the microphones were active; they were meant to pick up ambient sound. Practice streams will continue without audio.
Neither Pegula nor Andreeva had commented publicly. The WTA Finals run from 8 to 15 November at Indian Wells, Sky Sports said.

stories.head: Fritz and Paul keep ATP Finals hopes alive in Paris
stories.say: Taylor Fritz and Tommy Paul kept their ATP Finals hopes alive by reaching the Paris Masters quarter-finals. Fritz faces Carlos Alcaraz next, while Paul meets Ben Shelton.
stories.stand: Both Americans reached the Paris Masters quarter-finals as they chase the last two places at the season finale in Turin.
body: Americans Taylor Fritz and Tommy Paul reached the quarter-finals of the Paris Masters on Thursday, keeping alive their bids for the last places at the ATP Finals in Turin.

Fritz beat Frenchman Arthur Fils 6-3, 6-4 without facing a break point. The ATP said it was his 100th Masters 1000 win. He faces second seed Carlos Alcaraz on Friday, after Matteo Berrettini withdrew injured.
Paul beat Quentin Halys 7-6, 6-4 and will play Ben Shelton, who has already qualified for Turin. Shelton came from a set down to beat Arthur Rinderknech.
Two places remain. Fritz is 11th in the race, 184 points behind ninth-placed Rafael Jodar; Paul is 13th, 309 points behind.

stories.head: Scotland recall Huw Jones for All Blacks Test
stories.say: Scotland have recalled Huw Jones for Saturday's match against New Zealand at Murrayfield. They have never beaten the All Blacks, losing all 33 previous Tests.
stories.stand: Gregor Townsend's side face New Zealand at Murrayfield on Saturday, seeking a first win over the All Blacks in 33 Tests.
body: Scotland named their team on Thursday to face New Zealand in the Nations Championship at Murrayfield on Saturday. Kick-off is at 2.10pm.
Sione Tuipulotu captains the side from inside centre. British and Irish Lion Huw Jones returns at outside centre, with Blair Kinghorn on the bench. Finn Russell and Ben White start at half-back.
Scotland have not beaten the All Blacks in 33 Tests since the first meeting in 1905, RugbyPass reported. Head coach Gregor Townsend said he did not believe the run was about aura.
Elsewhere, Ireland play Argentina in Dublin on Friday, Wales face Japan on Saturday and England meet Australia on Sunday, Sky Sports reported.
